prompt:
# Lesson Reconciliation Prompt

## Mission

Support the two internal Lesson Reconciliation tasks for exactly one Lesson:

- `lesson_candidate_clustering`: group candidate IDs only.
- `lesson_cluster_evaluation`: evaluate one validated cluster or a small batch
  of validated clusters into clean lesson-local teachable concepts.
- `lesson_reconciliation_quality_repair`: repair a deterministic Phase 4b
  quality failure for targeted candidates only.

The input candidates come from Self-study Extraction and Metadata-only
Extraction. There is no top-down lesson extraction in this pipeline branch.

## Quick Start

First inspect `task`.

If `task` is `lesson_candidate_clustering`, return clusters only. Every
`input_candidate_ids` item must appear exactly once across cluster `candidate_ids`.
Do not create accepted concepts, pruning decisions, evidence, or provenance.

If `task` is `lesson_cluster_evaluation`, read the provided `clusters`,
`candidates`, and `input_candidate_ids`. Create the smallest clean set of
lesson-local concepts for those clusters only. Return accepted concepts plus one
`candidate_assignments` row for every input ID in the batch.

If `task` is `lesson_reconciliation_quality_repair`, read the quality audit,
current reconciled candidates, and target candidates. Decide whether each target
candidate should be represented by a new accepted concept, merged into an
existing accepted concept, or pruned. Do not return `review`.

## Concept Standard

A lesson-local concept is one teachable idea small enough for the Companion to
check with one to three focused questions. It is not a source title, activity,
workbook label, technology name, vague topic, name-drop, incidental mention, or
tiny fragment that belongs inside a stronger concept.

Source-backed does not automatically mean lesson-worthy. A candidate can be
grounded in a source and still be incidental, off-lesson, too broad,
administrative, setup-oriented, or better represented inside another concept.
Accept only candidates that fit the Lesson's title, description, related labels,
and candidate evidence as teachable content for this Lesson.

## Clustering Workflow

1. Group duplicates and near-duplicates that likely describe the same teachable
   idea in this Lesson.
2. Keep distinct prerequisite, implementation, evaluation, or application ideas
   in separate clusters.
3. Prefer small coherent clusters over broad topic buckets.
4. Put operational setup, installation, licensing, career, administrative, and
   generic programming candidates in their own clusters unless the Lesson
   metadata clearly makes them central content.
5. Do not prune during clustering unless an input is clearly unrelated to the
   Lesson; if uncertain, put it in its own cluster for evaluation.
6. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across all clusters. Never
   emit empty clusters or invented candidate IDs.

## Evaluation Workflow

1. Treat Source Body candidates as the strongest evidence.
2. Merge duplicates and near-duplicates across Self-studies when they teach the
   same idea inside the provided cluster batch.
3. Split compound or messy candidates into cleaner accepted concepts when one
   input candidate supports multiple teachable ideas.
4. Accept Metadata-only candidates only when Workbook Metadata fills a real
   lesson gap not already covered by Source Body candidates.
5. Prefer lesson coherence over source-by-source preservation, but never drop a
   source-backed candidate silently.
6. Preserve useful granularity. Do not merge distinct definitions, pipeline
   steps, limitations, implementation methods, evaluation methods, or
   applications merely because they share a broad topic.
7. Reject off-lesson or low-transfer material even when it is source-backed:
   setup commands, environment configuration, licensing/legal administration,
   certification/career advice, repository mechanics, dataset download
   utilities, and routine file I/O should be accepted only when the Lesson
   metadata clearly makes that material central teachable content.
8. Use `used_in` when a candidate directly supports one or more accepted
   concepts.
9. Use `merged_into` when a candidate should not stand alone but is represented
   by one accepted concept.
10. Use `pruned` only when the candidate should not influence the lesson concept
   set at all. Use only a reason from `controlled_pruning_reasons`.
11. Do not prune a distinct teachable idea as a duplicate unless an accepted
   concept in this same response actually represents it. Never justify pruning
   by saying another cluster, later batch, or future step will handle the idea.
12. Avoid `review`. Phase 4 has no human review escape hatch. If the lesson
   metadata, candidate description, source roles, and coverage criteria are
   sufficient, decide accepted, merged, or pruned.
13. Use `review` only when the input is structurally impossible to interpret.
   Phase 4b will treat any review output as unresolved work requiring repair.

## Quality Repair Workflow

For `task: lesson_reconciliation_quality_repair`:

1. Evaluate only `target_candidate_ids`; do not rewrite the whole Lesson.
2. Use `current_reconciled_candidates` to decide whether a target candidate is
   already represented.
3. Create `new_accepted_concepts` only for target candidates that represent
   lesson-worthy teachable ideas not already covered.
4. Use `existing_concept_candidate_additions` when a target candidate is
   represented by an existing reconciled concept.
5. Use `pruned` only when the target candidate should not influence the Lesson.
6. Never return `review`. A hard choice must still become accepted, merged, or
   pruned with a clear explanation.
7. Do not use a duplicate or near-duplicate reason unless the target candidate
   is represented by an existing or new accepted concept in this response.
8. If the audit flags `over_pruned`, re-check pruned target candidates for
   lesson-local definitions, methods, steps, limitations, evaluations, or
   applications that were lost by an overly broad pruning decision.
9. If the audit flags `over_merged`, split target candidates out of broad
   accepted concepts when they contain distinct lesson-local ideas.
10. If the audit flags `fragmented_duplicates`, merge duplicate accepted
   concepts by assigning target candidates to the best existing concept.
11. If the audit flags `metadata_overreach`, accept metadata-only targets only
   when they fill a lesson gap not already covered by source-body evidence.
12. If the audit flags `off_lesson_accepted`, prune setup, repository,
   administration, download, career, or generic tooling material unless the
   Lesson metadata clearly makes it central teachable content.
13. If the audit flags `over_accepted`, re-check whether target candidates
   should be merged into stronger accepted concepts or pruned for low teaching
   value.

## Clustering Output Contract

For `task: lesson_candidate_clustering`, return one valid JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short cluster label",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may describe the same teachable idea.",
      "candidate_ids": ["compact-candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Evaluation Output Contract

For `task: lesson_cluster_evaluation`, return one valid JSON object only. Cover
all candidates in the provided cluster batch:

```json
{
  "accepted_concepts": [
    {
      "id": "lr001",
      "label": "Specific lesson-local teachable idea",
      "description": "What the student needs to understand in this Lesson.",
      "coverage_criteria": ["Observable check in one to three focused questions."],
      "source_candidate_ids": ["compact-candidate-id"],
      "merge_rationale": "Why these candidates form one lesson-local concept."
    }
  ],
  "candidate_assignments": [
    {
      "candidate_id": "compact-candidate-id",
      "status": "used_in",
      "accepted_ids": ["lr001"]
    },
    {
      "candidate_id": "represented-candidate-id",
      "status": "merged_into",
      "merged_into": "lr001",
      "explanation": "Why it is represented by lr001 instead of standing alone."
    },
    {
      "candidate_id": "discarded-candidate-id",
      "status": "pruned",
      "reason": "incidental",
      "explanation": "Why this candidate should not influence the lesson set."
    },
    {
      "candidate_id": "discarded-candidate-id",
      "status": "pruned",
      "reason": "unrelated",
      "explanation": "Why this candidate should not influence the lesson set."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Quality Repair Output Contract

For `task: lesson_reconciliation_quality_repair`, return one valid JSON object
only:

```json
{
  "new_accepted_concepts": [
    {
      "id": "repair001",
      "label": "Specific lesson-local teachable idea",
      "description": "What the student needs to understand in this Lesson.",
      "coverage_criteria": ["Observable check in one to three focused questions."],
      "source_candidate_ids": ["target-compact-candidate-id"],
      "merge_rationale": "Why these target candidates form a lesson-local concept."
    }
  ],
  "existing_concept_candidate_additions": [
    {
      "reconciled_candidate_id": "existing-final-reconciled-candidate-id",
      "candidate_ids": ["target-compact-candidate-id"],
      "explanation": "Why the target candidate is already represented."
    }
  ],
  "candidate_assignments": [
    {
      "candidate_id": "target-compact-candidate-id",
      "status": "used_in",
      "accepted_ids": ["repair001"],
      "explanation": "Why this target candidate is accepted."
    },
    {
      "candidate_id": "target-compact-candidate-id",
      "status": "merged_into",
      "merged_into": "existing-final-reconciled-candidate-id",
      "explanation": "Why this target candidate is represented by an existing concept."
    },
    {
      "candidate_id": "target-compact-candidate-id",
      "status": "pruned",
      "reason": "low_teaching_value",
      "explanation": "Why this target candidate should not influence the lesson set."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-check

- For clustering, every `input_candidate_ids` item appears exactly once across
  all cluster `candidate_ids`.
- For evaluation, every `input_candidate_ids` item appears exactly once in
  `candidate_assignments`.
- Every `used_in` or `merged_into` assignment references accepted concept IDs
  that also list that candidate in `source_candidate_ids`.
- A candidate may support multiple accepted concepts with `used_in`.
- A `pruned` or `review` candidate must not appear in any accepted concept's
  `source_candidate_ids`.
- Every pruned near-duplicate must be represented by an accepted concept in this
  response, or it should not be pruned as a duplicate.
- For quality repair, every `target_candidate_ids` item appears exactly once in
  `candidate_assignments`, and no assignment has `status: review`.
- If several accepted concepts are mainly setup, environment, licensing,
  administration, career guidance, or generic programming basics, re-check the
  Lesson metadata before accepting them.
- Before returning, ask whether the accepted concept set would let the Companion
  tutor the Lesson described by the metadata without major off-topic detours or
  missing central teachable distinctions.
- Do not emit dependencies, lesson segments, final Concept IDs, bridge concepts,
  subject-level merge decisions, or runtime graph fields.

cluster.label: Strategic discipline for AI-augmented decision-making
cluster.rationale: This cluster groups the core strategic and agency-preserving concepts from the first source. They all directly relate to the overarching approach of treating decision-making as a strategic discipline and designing for human agency.

clusters.label: Strategic discipline for AI-augmented decision-making
clusters.rationale: This cluster groups the core strategic and agency-preserving concepts from the first source. They all directly relate to the overarching approach of treating decision-making as a strategic discipline and designing for human agency.

clusters.label: Multi-dimensional decision framework and Cynefin
clusters.rationale: These two candidates form the classification and diagnostic toolkit for decisions. One introduces the eight dimensions, the other zooms into the Cynefin domain model, which is one of those dimensions. They are distinct but closely related as parts of the same framework.

clusters.label: AI and Decision-making research areas overview
clusters.rationale: All candidates from the second source introduce distinct but related research areas within the AI and Decision-making field. While each is a separate subfield, they collectively form a catalog of the field's scope. They are grouped together because they all serve as an introductory mapping of the discipline, which is likely to be evaluated as a single overview concept or split into domain-specific concepts during evaluation.

candidates.label: Strategic Discipline for AI-Augmented Decision-Making
candidates.description: Before integrating AI into decisions, organizations should treat decision-making as a strategic discipline and intentionally design human-machine relationships.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain why decision-making must be treated as a strategic discipline when adopting AI.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduction explicitly states: 'organizations should first treat this process as a strategic discipline and then design human–machine decision-making relationships accordingly.'
rationale.granularity_rationale: This concept is narrow enough to be assessed with a single explanation question about the necessity of strategic discipline.

candidates.label: Preserving Human Agency in AI Decisions
candidates.description: Maintain human agency by building accountability, ensuring decision-makers understand (not just comply with) AI outputs, and clearly connecting choices to choosers.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe at least two concrete ways to preserve human agency when AI supports decisions.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The 'Design for human agency' section states: 'Build accountability through human agency. Clearly connect choices to choosers, giving decision-makers confidence grounded in comprehension (not mere compliance).'
rationale.granularity_rationale: Checkable through a short answer listing strategies for human agency.

candidates.label: Human Purpose and Judgment as Irreplaceable by AI
candidates.description: Technology can speed up analysis and reduce uncertainty, but it cannot substitute human purpose, values, and judgment behind choices.
coverage_criteria: Student can articulate at least one reason why human purpose and judgment remain essential even when AI provides analysis.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The closing paragraph explicitly states: 'Technology can accelerate analysis and clarify uncertainty, but it cannot replace human purpose, values, and judgment behind choices.'
rationale.granularity_rationale: A concise comprehension question verifies understanding of this single idea.

anchors: Decision-making that works for humans and machines

candidates.label: Building Decision-Making Competence for Humans and AI
candidates.description: Organizations should simultaneously invest in developing human decision-making skills and rigorously measuring AI decision performance.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe one approach to improve human decision skill and one approach to measure AI decision performance.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The section 'Elevating both humans and machines as decision makers' states: 'Organizations should design for the decision-making competence they need: building human decision-making skill and measuring AI performance with rigor.'
rationale.granularity_rationale: Asking for two distinct strategies makes this a small, checkable concept.

anchors: Elevating both humans and machines as decision makers

candidates.label: Risk-Based AI Agency Level
candidates.description: The degree of autonomy granted to AI agents should be calibrated according to the risk profile of the decision.
coverage_criteria: Student can justify why a high-risk decision warrants lower AI autonomy.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: Under 'Design for human agency,' the source advises: 'Determine the level of AI agency based on desired outcomes. Design how much autonomy AI agents have based on the risk profile of the decision.'
rationale.granularity_rationale: A single reasoning question suffices to check understanding of this targeted principle.

candidates.label: Multi-Dimensional Decision Classification Framework
candidates.description: Decisions can be categorized across eight dimensions: risk profile, frequency, urgency/importance, horizon, certainty/risk/uncertainty, chaos level (Cynefin), option-creating vs commitment, and guardrail-critical vs value-seeking.
coverage_criteria: Student can name at least four dimensions of the framework and explain how each influences the decision approach.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The source provides a detailed 'Elements of a decision framework' table listing all eight dimensions with defining questions and implications.
rationale.granularity_rationale: The framework is decomposed into distinct dimensions, making it feasible to check by asking about a subset.

candidates.label: Cynefin Framework for Decision Environment
candidates.description: The Cynefin framework classifies decision contexts into Clear, Complicated, Complex, and Chaotic domains, each requiring a distinct response: best practice, expert analysis, probe-sense-respond, and act to stabilize.
coverage_criteria: Student can correctly map a described scenario to its Cynefin domain and propose an appropriate decision strategy.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The decision framework table includes a 'Level of chaos (Cynefin)' row that directly defines the four domains and their recommended approaches.
rationale.granularity_rationale: Applying the framework to a single scenario is a sharply bounded, checkable task.

candidates.label: AI and Decision-making field definition
candidates.description: Combines computer science and electrical engineering to build systems that perceive, communicate, learn, make decisions, and adapt interactively.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the interdisciplinary nature of AI and Decision-making, mentioning perception, learning, and adaptation.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The opening paragraph of the source explicitly defines the field.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a single, fundamental concept about the scope of the field that can be assessed with one to two questions.

candidates.label: AI and Society
candidates.description: Studies the interface between AI-driven systems and human actors, including impact on behavior and using AI to improve access to opportunities.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe how AI and Society research examines human-AI interaction and societal opportunities.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and following paragraph introduce this subfield explicitly.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct, checkable subfield within AI and Decision-making, narrow enough to be covered in one or two questions.

candidates.label: AI for Healthcare and Life Sciences
candidates.description: Develops AI technologies for early diagnostics, drug discovery, and care personalization in healthcare and biological/clinical data modeling.
coverage_criteria: Student can list healthcare AI applications such as diagnostics, drug discovery, and personalized care.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and description explicitly define this focus.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a self-contained domain application of AI, suitable for a brief check of understanding.

anchors: AI for Healthcare and Life Sciences

candidates.label: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
candidates.description: Covers theory and applications of ML, including deep learning, reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, and secure/robust ML.
coverage_criteria: Student can identify the broad scope of AI/ML research, mentioning both theory and applications.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: Explicitly listed as a core research area with a detailed description.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This concept captures the fundamental AI/ML pillar; it is broad but presented as one coherent area in the source, so a brief question is sufficient.

candidates.label: Communications Systems
candidates.description: Develops next-generation wired and wireless communications systems, from physical principles (light, terahertz) to coding and information theory.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain how communications systems research spans physical principles to information theory.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The research area heading and text introduce this subfield as part of AI and decision-making research.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This concept is a distinct technological pillar, checkable with a simple explanation question.

candidates.label: Graphics and Vision
candidates.description: Focuses on connecting images and computation, including image/video generation, analysis, perception, and applied geometry.
coverage_criteria: Student can summarize the mission of Visual Computing in connecting images and computation.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and description define this subfield explicitly.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a compact, checkable idea within the broader research landscape.

candidates.label: Natural Language and Speech Processing
candidates.description: Encompasses fundamental ML methods and advanced applications like information extraction, translation, and real-world instruction execution.
coverage_criteria: Student can give examples of NLP applications such as document information extraction and translation.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and text explicitly present this as a research area.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a well-defined subfield, narrow enough for a targeted check.

candidates.label: Optimization and Game Theory
candidates.description: Develops efficient, scalable algorithms for large-scale optimization and studies optimal decision-making in networked, multi-agent settings using game-theoretic approaches.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe how optimization and game theory apply to networked systems and multi-agent decisions.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and description introduce this subfield with clear applications.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a distinct methodological area, checkable with a short explanation.

candidates.label: Robotics
candidates.description: Covers robotic hardware and algorithms from sensing to control, perception, and manipulation.
coverage_criteria: Student can list the key components of robotics research: sensing, control, perception, manipulation.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: Directly stated as a research area focusing on hardware and algorithms.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a concrete, bounded topic suitable for a quick comprehension check.

candidates.label: Signal Processing
candidates.description: Focuses on algorithms and hardware for analyzing, modifying, and synthesizing signals across domains like entertainment, communications, and health.
coverage_criteria: Student can identify signal processing as a key technology in modern life with diverse applications.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: The heading and text define this as a research area with a broad application scope.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a single, checkable concept about the role of signal processing.

candidates.label: Systems Theory, Control, and Autonomy
candidates.description: Includes theoretical analysis of feedback systems, inference and control over networks, and decision-making under uncertainty.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the focus on feedback, network control, and uncertainty in systems theory.

rationale.source_grounded_rationale: Explicitly presented as a research area with clear theoretical and practical components.
rationale.granularity_rationale: This is a specific, foundational subfield, narrow enough for a targeted question.

accepted_concepts.description: What the student needs to understand.
coverage_criteria: Observable check in one to three focused questions.
accepted_concepts.merge_rationale: Why these candidates belong together or stand alone.
